text:
anya: seeing weird decode quality blips and ~20-60ms tail latency spikes on FP8 KV paths after yesterday's kernel selection change. Only on p3-like nodes, not on small-test GPU pool.

sam: :eyes: do you have a run id / example input?

anya: run 2026-03-kvcal-42. Short repro: long-context chat prompt (10k tokens) + streaming. When we hit cache-hits > 90% the decode sometimes inserts junk tokens and latency jumps.

mike: can you paste the profiler snippets? might be kernel fallback or an alignment issue with int8->fp8 page walker.

anya: pasted minimal traces below (sanitized):
```
$ perf-profile --run 2026-03-kvcal-42 --filters kv
KVCache::read  t=0.0s  size=6.2GB  hits=92%  kernel=fp8_kv_pagewalker_v2
KVCache::decode t=0.012s  kernel=int8_decode_v3 fallback=fp8_mixed_path
decode-step  token_idx=12000  latency=0.098s  stall=0.045s
...
```

julia: hm fallback=fp8_mixed_path while kernel set to fp8_kv_pagewalker_v2 — that mismatch smells like opportunistic kernel switch when batch size crosses threshold. Might be heuristic in kernel_selector.

sam: if kernel_selector flips mid-request you can get inconsistent quant scales which would explain quality blips. Do we have calibration tables applied per-kernel or global?

anya: we use per-model calibration artifacts, but selector caches kernel metadata per-device. After the deploy the selector started preferring fp8 for large prefixes; it still allowed int8 decode kernels for certain logits ops. Calibration files are: modelX.fp8.calib.v3 and modelX.int8.calib.v2.

mike: quick check — can you run a trace that forces kernel pinned to fp8_kv_pagewalker_v2 for the whole request and compare?

anya: ran a quick A/B:
```
# pinned -> stable decode, no junk tokens, avg latency tail 45ms
$ run --kernel-preset=fp8_pin --run 2026-03-kvcal-42
# default selector -> junk ~3% of requests, avg tail 120ms
$ run --kernel-preset=auto --run 2026-03-kvcal-42
```

anya: attaching reduced logs (inline) showing token drift when selector toggles: 
```
... token: "San Francisco" -> "San Frnacisco"
... token: "3.14" -> "3.140000e+00"
```

julia: that token-level corruption strongly implies differing quant scale / dequant rounding between the two kernels. Have we validated calibration using the long-context distribution? Old calibration runs were with 2k seq, not 10k.

sam: good catch. Calibration on long-prefix workloads can shift per-head scaling. We should rerun per-kernel calibration with long-context traces and then force the selector to pick a single codepath for now.

infra-bot: rollback-ready patch queued: revert kernel_selector change (PR #3821). CI perf tests green.

mike: steps I propose: 1) pin kernel to fp8 for affected fleet, 2) regenerate calibration tables using long-context traces, 3) add selector safety check to avoid mid-request kernel swap, 4) add telemetry label when fallback happens so we can alert on rate > 0.1%.

anya: implementing 1 and 4 now. Pin patch deployed to canary 3.

sam: also add a fast invariant check in decode that asserts consistent quant-scale metadata across ops at start of request — log and increment counter if mismatch. Keep it opt-in behind debug flag.

julia: also check GPU page alignment: I saw a subtle bug earlier where fp8 kernel expects 512B-aligned pages, int8 expects 256B. When the allocator defragged across allocations the same buffer got different alignment hints and selector saw it as compatible but ops misread stride. Could cause jittery stalls.

anya: ran canary for 30m: no junk tokens, tail latency stable. Rolling to 20% fleet now.

mike: once calibration tables are updated let's run mixed stress: varying batch sizes, streaming on/off, and long-token-prefixes to ensure selector heuristics don't flip at edge thresholds. Add coverage for p3-like and a100 pools.

sam: logging TODOs: add telemetry field kv_quant_switch=true when a kernel fallback happens, and histogram of per-request token-ppm corrupted (sanity check).

anya: noted. I'll attach the per-request diff tool we used to quantify corruption rate. Quick command: `python tools/kv_diff.py --gold gold.out --run out.log --metric word-edit-distance`

julia: thanks. If we see any residuals after recalibration, schedule a kernel dev sync — the fp8 implementation may need rounding-mode harmonization with int8 path.

infra-bot: deploy status: canary->20% (2026-03-18T14:22:11Z).

mike: great. For the postmortem, capture: root cause hypothesis (selector-induced kernel mix + calibration mismatch + allocation alignment), mitigation (pin selectors, regen calibrations, guardrails), and monitoring changes.

anya: will open an incident note and link to this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
